anu-p01.speaker: author (devotional voice)
anu-p01.question: Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.
premises: Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing.
This becomes śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone.
Reality free of void and non-void: the śāmbhava state.
anu-p01.inference: Dissolution, not effort, becomes the mudrā; grace alone, reality beyond extremes.
uncertainties: Whether śāmbhavī mudrā is performed or occurring is unresolved.

anu-p02.speaker: author (devotional voice)
anu-p02.question: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.
premises: Four outer strokes: half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved.
Then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person.
After which speech ends: what more is to be said?
anu-p02.inference: Portrait, then vision, then silence: recognition completes itself.
uncertainties: Whether the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva) is breath or consciousness is unresolved.

anu-p03.speaker: author (devotional voice)
anu-p03.question: No technique enjoined: whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra, whatever the body postures is already mudrā, whatever the breath's flow is already wonderful yoga — so, in the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?
premises: Whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra.
Whatever postures is already mudrā; whatever breath flows is already wonderful yoga.
In the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?
anu-p03.inference: No technique enjoined; recognition, not practice.
uncertainties: Whether 'śākta dhāma' means the abode of Śakti or the abode of the śākta is unresolved.

anu-p04.speaker: author (devotional voice)
anu-p04.question: Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.
premises: Mantra: where letters are not distinguished.
Mudrā: where bodily action is dissolved; yoga: where breath-flow is exhausted.
In the festivals of attaining Your abode, everything is wonderful.
anu-p04.inference: Each sacred form defined by what drops out; festival of the abode.
uncertainties: Whether 'sudhī' means 'the wise' or 'the good-minded' is unresolved.

anu-p01.plain_english: When the yogin abides with mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim — he, seeing yet not seeing outside with unmoving-pupil gaze — this indeed becomes the śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: devoid of void and non-void becomes that reality, the śāmbhava state.
anu-p01.sanskrit_cite: antarlakṣyavilīnacittapavanaḥ yogī yadā vartate dṛṣṭyā niścalatārayā bahir asau paśyan apaśyan api mudreyam | khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā yuṣmatprasādāt guro śūnyāśūnyavivarjitam bhavati yat tattvam padam śāmbhavam

anu-p02.plain_english: Half-open-eyed, steady-minded, gaze placed on the nose-tip — moon and sun too have attained dissolution in the interior of the triple-throb state — light-formed, devoid of all exteriority, and one supreme person: reality attains that state, the thing supreme. What more is there to say here?
anu-p02.sanskrit_cite: ardhoddhāṭitalocanaḥ sthiramanāḥ nāsāgradattekṣaṇaḥ candrārkau api līnatām upagatau trispandabhāvāntare jyotīrūpam aśeṣabāhyarahitam ca ekam | pumāṃsam param tattvam tat padam eti vastu paramam vācyam kim atra adhikam

anu-p03.plain_english: Whatever sound arises from the mouth — that mantra is transcendent. Whatever posture of the pleasure-pain-born body — that indeed is mudrā. Whatever flowing of breath by its own rhythm — that indeed is wonderful yoga. The supreme śākta abode — while I experience, what indeed would not shine?
anu-p03.sanskrit_cite: śabdaḥ kaścana yaḥ mukhāt udayate mantraḥ saḥ lokottaraḥ saṃsthānam sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣaḥ yat kāpi mudrā eva sā prāṇasya | svarasena yat pravahaṇam yogaḥ saḥ eva adbhutaḥ śāktam dhāma param mamānubhavataḥ kim nāma na bhrājate

anu-p04.plain_english: That mantra shines forth in which letter-arrangement is not distinguished. That mudrā arises in which entire bodily action is dissolved. That yoga spreads forth from which breath's flowing is exhausted. In the festivals of attaining Your abode, of the wise — what, what is indeed not wonderful? *Fidelity: preserved (all 4 verses, full pādas from T1). Added: connective phrasing only. Not-resolved: trispandabhāva read as inhalation/exhalation/juncture (marked); yataḥ read relatively; śāktaṃ dhāma read as nominative.*
anu-p04.sanskrit_cite: mantraḥ saḥ pratibhāti varṇa racanā yasmin na saṃlakṣyate mudrā sā samudeti yatra galitā kṛtsnā kriyā | kāyikī yogaḥ saḥ prathate yataḥ pravahaṇam prāṇasya saṃkṣīyate tvaddhāmādhigamotsaveṣu sudhiyām kim kim na nāma adbhutam

essence: Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (adbhuta), integrated into the śāmbhava state.

essence: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of vision (darśana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the light-form person.

essence: No technique enjoined: whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra, whatever the body postures is already mudrā, whatever the breath's flow is already wonderful yoga — so, in the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?

rasa.sthayibhava: ānanda (bliss) as everything is already yoga
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of recognition (pratyabhijñā); the vyabhicāri is joy (harṣa) that all utterance/posture/breath is already mantra/mudrā/yoga.

essence: Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as the festival of the abode
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of festival (utsava); the vyabhicāri is wonder (adbhuta) that everything is wonderful for the wise.

lines: When the yogin rests, mind and breath dissolved in the inward aim — seeing, yet unseeing, outward with motionless gaze —
this indeed becomes śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: reality free of void and non-void becomes the śāmbhava state.
anu-p01.sanskrit_cite: antarlakṣyavilīnacittapavano yogī yadā vartate dṛṣṭyā niścalatārayā bahirasau paśyannapaśyannapi | mudreyaṃ khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā yuṣmatprasādādguro śūnyāśūnyavivarjitaṃ bhavati yat tattvaṃ padaṃ śāmbhavam

lines: Eyes half-open, mind steady, gaze set on the nose-tip — moon and sun themselves dissolved within the triple throb —
a form of light, free of all outside, the one supreme Person: reality attains that state, the highest Real. so it stands, past saying.
anu-p02.sanskrit_cite: ardhoddhāṭitalocanaḥ sthiramanā nāsāgradattekṣaṇaḥ candrārkāvapi līnatāmupagatau trispandabhāvāntare | jyotīrūpamaśeṣabāhyarahitaṃ caikaṃ pumāṃsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tatpadameti vastu paramam vācyaṃ kimatrādhikam

lines: Whatever sound rises from the mouth — that mantra is beyond the world; whatever stance this pleasure-pain-born body takes — that itself is mudrā.
Whatever flowing of breath in its own rhythm — that itself is wondrous yoga; and the supreme śākta abode — as I experience it, what would not shine?
anu-p03.sanskrit_cite: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
notes: śākta kept transliterated (of-Śakti vs of-the-śākta open)

lines: That mantra shines where no pattern of letters can be traced; that mudrā rises where every bodily act has melted away.
That yoga spreads where the breath’s flowing is spent; in the festivals of attaining Your abode, of the wise — what, what is not wonderful?
anu-p04.sanskrit_cite: mantraḥ sa pratibhāti varṇaracanā yasminna saṃlakṣyate mudrā sā samudeti yatra galitā kṛtsnā kriyā kāyikī | yogaḥ sa prathate yataḥ pravahaṇaṃ prāṇasya saṃkṣīyate tvaddhāmādhigamotsaveṣu sudhiyāṃ kiṃ kiṃ na nāmādbhutaṃ
notes: sudhī kept genitive (‘of the wise’); vocative reading open

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as śāmbhavī mudrā with adbhuta; sthāyibhāva bhakti in the mode of pratyabhijñā (recognition), vyabhicāri wonder (C1 rasa block). Verse color: paradox held steady resolving into grace-given recognition. Firing structures: the oxymoron paśyan/apaśyan is given by the source and is the verse's hinge -> isolate 'seeing, yet unseeing' on its own line (the eye stops where the gaze stops); the long opening bahuvrīhi (antarlakṣyavilīnacittapavanaḥ) is one inward breath -> first line unbroken; vocative turn (guro) -> colon address; terminal doctrine word (śāmbhavam) -> end-weight the state name. Dashes as chant breaths. Minimal pass: reline L3 into breath units + paradox-pivot device; no diction changes beyond L3's own words.

notes.craft_notes: Same work voice as anu v1 (quatrain, dash breaths); new song, new sthāyin: adbhuta as the vision unfolds — bhakti in the mode of darśana, vyabhicāri camatkāra at the light-form person (C1 rasa block). Verse color: portrait, then vision, then silence. Firing rows: three parallel bahuvrīhi portrait-strokes -> parallel placement kept in one gathering line (row 3); compounds unpacked across the line-break (row 2); the close is the rupture AND the śānta-fall — Sanskrit ends not in statement but in question (vācyam kim atra adhikam, 'what more is to be said here?'). L3 states it ('past saying'); L4 restores the question: the verse silences itself by asking. Sanskrit-wins correction recorded here per ultimate-authority rule. FULL-LAYER AUDIT (all former layers re-read): L0 has no forks (all fork:none, single backfilled options) — it confirms rather than redirects: dual candrārkau (p003) + api too/even (p004) → 'themselves' carries both number and inclusion; pumāṃsam (p012) is accusative, the OBJECT of the vision → line 3 correctly an object-phrase, not subject; līnatām (p005, noun 'dissolvedness') + upagatau (p006, 'attained') → 'dissolved' collapse loses no aspect; atra (p022, 'here') absorbed into English 'there' — conscious thinning, vowel-arc cost of terminal 'here' judged higher than the deictic loss, recorded not hidden. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 close 'so it stands, past saying.' → killed by Sanskrit interrogative kim (L0 p021) + NOTE 'the question is the period': stating what the verse asks drops a rank and kills the rupture. (b) Close with atra kept ('...to say here?') → killed by vowel arc: terminal 'here' lifts where 'say' settles; 'there' absorbs the deixis. (c) Portrait strokes split over two lines → killed by row 3: the three bahuvrīhis are one gathering breath, splitting flattens the parallel placement and breaks v1's quatrain-breath voice. (d) 'tip of the nose' → killed by row 2 density + singability; L3's hyphen-chain 'nose-tip' stands. (e) 'too' for api ('moon and sun too dissolved') → killed by economy: 'themselves' carries dual number + inclusion in one word. (f) Line-3 colon (L3's ':') → killed by voice continuity: v1 set dash-breaths, a colon would import a second caesura system. End-weight: the question is line-final and song-final — speech ends where the line ends. Vowel arc bright (Eyes, light) to dark (say). Read aloud: three long gathering lines, one short closing question — the breath stops where speech stops.

notes.craft_notes: Same work voice (quatrain, dash breaths); new song, new sthāyin: ānanda as everything-is-already-yoga — bhakti in the mode of pratyabhijñā (recognition), vyabhicāri harṣa (joy that all utterance/posture/breath is already mantra/mudrā/yoga). Verse color: recognition over technique; nothing enjoined, everything shining. Firing rows: the source's own engine is threefold repetition-with-variation (yat…saḥ / yat…sā / yat…saḥ, row 9) → English anaphora, capital 'Whatever' line-initial ×3; verb-final bhrājate (row 1) → end-weight 'shine' line-final and song-final; close is interrogative kim…na bhrājate (L0 p027) → the question IS the close again (v2's principle holds: the question is the period), but here it affirms — 'what would NOT shine?' means everything shines, so the vowel arc runs bright-to-brightest, the inverse of v2's dark settle. First-person mama (L0 p026) kept as 'I' per row 11 deixis: the Sanskrit particularizes, so English particularizes — generalizing to 'one' would betray the trace. FULL-LAYER AUDIT: L0 no forks (all fork:none); three redefinitions map cleanly p000–p007 (sound→mantra), p008–p014 (posture→mudrā), p015–p022 (breath-flow→yoga); śākta kept transliterated per L3 note (abode-of-Śakti vs of-the-śākta open — do not resolve in song). NOTE confirms 'Nothing enjoined; utterance, posture, breathing are recognized as already mantra, mudrā, yoga' + 'shining is the default' — the draft's arc is the analysis sung. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 couplet kept as 2 long lines → killed by work voice (v1/v2 quatrain) + row 9: anaphora needs line-initial repetition to scan, three redefinitions need three breaths. (b) lowercase mid-line 'whatever' → killed by the device itself: unstressed repetition isn't anaphora. (c) 'transcendent' for lokottara (L0 gloss) → killed by rule 15 + singability: L3's 'beyond the world' is frozen and breathes; both trace p007. (d) dropping line-4 'and' → killed by small-edits rule: L3's joint, keep it. (e) 'while I experience' (L2) over L3's 'as I experience it' → killed by L3-frozen; both trace p026. (f) declarative close ('everything shines.') → killed by kim interrogative + v2 precedent: stating what the verse asks drops the rank. Read aloud: three gathering Whatever-lines, one bright closing question — the breath opens, not stops.

notes.craft_notes: Work voice holds (quatrain, dash breaths); closing song of the work, sthāyin: śānta as the festival of the abode — bhakti in the mode of utsava (festival), vyabhicāri adbhuta that everything is wonderful for the wise. Verse color: definitions by vanishing erupting into festival (v3 said all IS yoga; v4 says each form is known by what has dropped out of it — recognition deepens). Firing rows: strict yasmin/yatra/yataḥ parallel (rows 3+9) → 'That…where…' anaphora ×3, the structural rhyme answering v3's 'Whatever ×3'; three DISTINCT verbs pratibhāti/samudeti/prathate → kept distinct (each form shines differently — variety is doctrine); doubled kim kim (L0 p025–p026) → the stammer kept, it IS the camatkāra; tvad second person (row 7) → 'Your' prominent, distance collapsed; sudhī open (BOUNDARY) → L3's 'of the wise' kept, note carried. FULL-LAYER AUDIT: L0 no forks; NOTE's 'Three definitions by vanishing, in strict yasmin/yatra/yataḥ parallel' + 'it ends in festival' is the draft's skeleton — analysis sung, not decorated. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 couplet kept → killed by work-voice quatrain + three definitions need three breaths. (b) flattening shines/arises/spreads to one verb → killed by Sanskrit: three verbs, three musics; flattening sanitizes variety. (c) single 'what' (smoothing the stammer) → killed by doubled kim kim: undoubling calms the camatkāra. (d) resolving sudhī to 'the good-minded' → killed by BOUNDARY (unresolved). (e) 'dissolved' for galitā over L3's 'melted away' → killed by rule 15, L3 frozen; both trace p012. (f) exclamatory close ('how wonderful!') → killed by v2 precedent + row 10: the question affirms, exclamation states. Read aloud: three That-lines gathering by vanishing, one festival question — the song ends open, shining.
